title: 11 demands rejection of the LRM's own shiftPlus5; make it a RUN fixture
detail: ch1-intro.html lines 60-70 print shiftPlus5 (input/output ports, potential-only discipline, V(out) <+ 5.0 + V(in)) as a legal normative example. The fixture transcribes it and asserts `//! reject GeneratedCompileError`, a VerA backend phase (torture.zig:565 'codegen deliberately emitted @compileError'). VERIFIED: `vera --lint` on the fixture is silent (front end accepts); `vera --emit-zig` refuses. VERIFIED the refusal is generic, not about custom access names: I wrote the LRM's exact source using the Annex D prelude disciplines (src/frontend/preprocessor.zig:1108 declares `discipline voltage; potential Voltage; enddiscipline`) and codegen refused that too, at codegen.zig:838 signalFlowNet(), which refuses any contribution whose net is a directional port with a single-nature discipline. So a conformant compiler FAILS this fixture and VerA passes it. CORRECTION to the uncovered lens: tb.zig unknownName() strips only `V(`, `I(` and `x[` (tb.zig:234), NOT an arbitrary access wrapper, so a `//! bias SV(inp)=..` line would not resolve; use the Annex D `voltage` discipline and plain V(), which does.
expected: Delete the reject line and the sidecar. Body = the LRM's own module: `voltage in, out;` with input/output ports. Directives `//! lrm 1.3.4.1` and `//! bias V(in) = 1.25`. Assert `CHECKX("level-shifted output", 5.0 + V(in), 6.25)` (5.0+1.25=6.25, both dyadic, exact in binary64 - verified). Do NOT assert V(out): out is the potential-source branch unknown and reads the harness bias, not the contributed value. BLOCKED BY ch01-W04: as a run fixture it FAILs today because codegen refuses signal-flow nets; the runner has no xfail for run fixtures (tb.zig:206 `if (d.xfail != null and reject.items.len == 0) return error.XfailWithoutReject`). CORRECTION to the weak lens: it cannot be routed through CANNOT RUN either - torture.zig:798 matches only the `num_ports must be in 1..|U|` contract message.

title: 12 demands rejection of the LRM's own currmir; make it a RUN fixture
detail: ch1-intro.html lines 77-87 print currmir (input/output ports, flow-only discipline, I(out) <+ -I(in)) as legal. The fixture transcribes it and asserts `//! reject GeneratedCompileError`. VERIFIED identically to W01: front end silent, codegen refuses at signalFlowNet(); the Annex D `discipline current; flow Current; enddiscipline` spelling is refused the same way, so custom access names are not the cause.
expected: `//! lrm 1.3.4.2`, drop the reject and the sidecar, write the LRM's module with `current in, out;`. Hold the input flow and assert `CHECKX("the mirror negates the input flow", -I(in), -0.125)` (IEEE-754 negation is exact; 0.125 is dyadic). NOTE the directive needed here is a `//! sweep` of the branch-flow unknown, whose only spelling today is VerA's mangled `flowZ28inZ29` - see ch01-W23; fix that first or the fixture ships an implementation leak. Same W04 blocker as ch01-W01.

title: 13 demands rejection of the one thing 1.3.5 exists to guarantee; make it a RUN fixture
detail: ch1-intro.html line 127: 'Conservative components and signal-flow components can be freely mixed.' (line 92: '...arbitrarily mixed in the same system'). The fixture mixes a potential-only port with an inout electrical port and asserts `//! reject GeneratedCompileError`, i.e. it requires a compiler to reject the clause it cites. COVERAGE.md says so outright: 'its generated-code failure records VerA's present custom-access ABI boundary'. VERIFIED: front end accepts, codegen refuses (same signalFlowNet path).
expected: `//! lrm 1.3.5`, drop the reject and the sidecar, `//! bias V(p) = 2.0` and `//! bias` the signal-flow net. Assert on RHS expressions only: `CHECKX("scale factor k is 1e3", 1k, 1000.0)` and `CHECK("flow driven by the conservative probe", V(p)/1k, 2.0e-3, 1e-15)` (2.0/1000.0 == 2e-3 exactly - verified). Do not assert MV(sig) on the RHS: it is a potential-source branch unknown. Same W04 blocker.

title: Gating: the runner has no xfail for RUN fixtures, so W01-W03 and W15 cannot land honestly
detail: VERIFIED in code: tb.zig parse() returns error.XfailWithoutReject when `//! xfail` appears without `//! reject`, and torture.zig's CANNOT RUN verdict matches exactly one string, the `num_ports must be in 1..|U|` contract refusal (torture.zig:798). Everything else that fails to build is a hard FAIL. So the four fixtures the LRM requires to COMPILE (shiftPlus5, currmir, the mixed model, and the flow-antisymmetry check) have no home: keeping `//! reject` encodes a false requirement, and dropping it turns them red. This is the single decision the rest of the chapter's top block waits on.
expected: Either (a) allow `//! xfail <reason>` on a run fixture - the fixture must run and pass, VerA is known not to yet, XPASS stays a hard FAIL exactly as for rejects; or (b) fix codegen.zig:838 signalFlowNet() so single-nature directional nets lower. (a) is the small diff; (b) is the real fix and makes four fixtures go green instead of yellow. Also update tests/fixtures/README.md's xfail section.

title: 14 is rejected by the parser, not by 1.3.4; rewrite it as the real flow-onto-a-potential-only-net negative
detail: VERIFIED by running the compiler: `vera --lint 14_signal_flow_illegal_quantity.va` reports `error[E0209]: expected an expression: found `flow`` at the `flow(outp)` token. `flow` is a discipline-item keyword (A.1.7), not an access function, so the file dies in the parser and never reaches 1.3.4's rule; the same error would fire on a legal `electrical` net. Its expectation is the bare phase label `DiagnosticsReported`, which any rejection for any reason satisfies, and it carries no `//! lrm`. The rule it claims - ch1-intro.html line 56, 'If a node is bound only to disciplines which have potential nature only, current contributions to that node are not legal' - IS writable in one module with the Annex D `voltage` discipline, and VERIFIED VerA accepts the violation silently: `voltage vonly; analog I(vonly) <+ 1.0e-3;` lints clean and emits clean. Root cause per the negatives lens, confirmed in source: lower.zig checkAccessMatch returns early on `want.len == 0` ('Silent when the discipline binds no nature for that half').
expected: //! lrm 1.3.4 + //! reject <a new diagnostic code for 'the discipline binds no flow nature for this net'> + //! xfail (checkAccessMatch's want.len==0 early return accepts every flow access on a potential-only net). Body: `voltage vonly; analog begin I(vonly) <+ 1.0e-3; I(p) <+ V(p)*1.0e-3; end`. Delete the sidecar. Never re-use the bare phase label.

title: 10 sweeps a branch-flow unknown that a flow-source branch does not have; its wants are read off VerA internals
detail: The branch `measured` carries `I(measured) <+ 2.0*I(measured)`, which makes it a flow source (5.4.2.2). For a flow source the branch flow is the contributed, retained value (5.6.1.2/5.6.1.3), not a free unknown a host can pin - that degree of freedom exists only for a POTENTIAL source, which is why 05_potential_and_flow.va is legitimate and this is not. The wants 5.0e-3 / 1.0e-2 are the swept value echoed back through VerA's internal `flow(p,n)` unknown; the fixture's own comment concedes the model's only consistent solution is zero. Independently, got and want are the same number routed through the directive parser and the source, so the first CHECK cannot fail for a language reason. Arithmetic itself is fine (2.0*0.005 == 0.01 exactly).
expected: Make the probed branch a potential source, which is the LRM's own resistor: keep the sweep, replace the contribution with `V(measured) <+ 200.0 * I(measured);` and keep `CHECK("flow probe of the named branch", I(measured), 5.0e-3, 1e-15)` / `CHECKX("doubled flow", 2.0*I(measured), 1.0e-2)`. Cite `//! lrm 1.3.1` and `//! lrm 5.4.2.2`. Alternative, cheaper: delete the file - 05 already covers a flow probe on a source branch and ch05_analog_behavior/source_probe_both.va covers the named-branch form.

title: Missing negative: a potential signal-flow net bound to an inout port
detail: ch1-intro.html line 73, verbatim: 'Nets of potential signal flow disciplines in modules may only be bound to input or output ports of the module, not to inout ports.' Nothing in the suite declares a single-nature net on an inout. VERIFIED VerA accepts it end to end: `module m(p); inout p; voltage p; analog V(p) <+ 1.0; endmodule` lints clean AND emits clean - codegen.zig:837 says so in a comment ('A single-nature discipline on an inout port or on an internal net is NOT caught here'). Cheapest negative in the chapter: no analog statement is even needed to violate it.
expected: //! lrm 1.3.4.1 + //! reject <new code> + //! xfail (lower.zig records port direction at :554 only so codegen can refuse; nothing rejects inout on a single-nature discipline). Use the Annex D `voltage` discipline so the fixture reads like the LRM.

title: Missing negative: a flow signal-flow net bound to an inout port
detail: ch1-intro.html line 90, verbatim: 'Nets of flow signal-flow disciplines in modules may only be bound to input or output ports of the module, not to inout ports.' Mirror of W07. VERIFIED accepted: `module m(p); inout p; current p; analog I(p) <+ 1.0e-3; endmodule` emits clean.
expected: //! lrm 1.3.4.2 + //! reject <new code> + //! xfail, same shape as W07 with the Annex D `current` discipline.

title: Missing negative: a potential contribution made to an input port of a potential signal-flow net
detail: ch1-intro.html line 73, second sentence: 'In that case, potential contributions may not be made to input ports.' Distinct from W07 - the declaration is legal, the contribution is not. VERIFIED: `input inp; voltage inp; analog V(inp) <+ 1.0;` passes the front end silently; only codegen refuses, and it refuses for the generic signal-flow reason, so the fixture must NOT pin GeneratedCompileError - it would pass for the wrong reason and would keep passing after codegen learns to lower signal-flow nets.
expected: //! lrm 1.3.4.1 + //! reject <new front-end code for 'contribution to an input port'> + //! xfail (no front-end diagnostic distinguishes an input from an output contribution target).

title: Missing negative: a flow contribution made to an input port of a flow signal-flow net
detail: ch1-intro.html line 90, second sentence: 'Flow contributions may not be made to input ports in this case.' Mirror of W09, same verified silence in the front end.
expected: //! lrm 1.3.4.2 + //! reject <new code> + //! xfail, mirror of W09 with `current`.

title: Missing negative: a potential contribution onto a flow-only net (the 'conversely' half of 1.3.4)
detail: ch1-intro.html line 56: 'Conversely, if a node is bound only to disciplines which have flow nature only, potential contributions to that node are not legal. Potential for such a node is not defined.' W05 rewrites fixture 14 into the first half; this is the mirror and exists nowhere. VERIFIED accepted: `current ionly; analog V(ionly) <+ 1.0;` lints clean and emits clean.
expected: //! lrm 1.3.4 + //! reject <same new code family as W05> + //! xfail (checkAccessMatch early return, mirrored). Keep it a separate file from W05 so the runner reports which half fired.

title: Missing negative: both quantities of a PROBE branch appearing in expressions
detail: ch1-intro.html line 32, verbatim: 'The potential and flow of a probe branch may not both appear in expressions in a given module.' The rule bites only when nothing is contributed to the branch; the near-miss, ch05_analog_behavior/source_probe_both.va, contributes `V(b) <+ 10.0*I(b)`, so its branch is a source and it is legal. VERIFIED VerA accepts the violation: `branch (p,n) probe; analog I(o) <+ V(probe) + I(probe);` lints clean and emits clean.
expected: //! lrm 1.3.1 + //! reject <new code> + //! xfail (lower.zig never correlates the two accesses of an uncontributed node pair). The comment must state why the branch is a probe - it is never on the left of a `<+` - or a later reader will 'fix' it into a legal source branch.

title: Missing negative: both the potential and the flow of one SOURCE branch specified simultaneously
detail: Second half of the same sentence (ch1-intro.html line 32). The four V+I pairs in ch05_analog_behavior are all conditional, i.e. the legal 5.6.5 switch branch. VERIFIED VerA accepts the unconditional form: `analog begin V(p,n) <+ 1.0; I(p,n) <+ 1.0e-3; end` lints clean and emits clean; lower.zig contribIndex treats any V+I pair on one node pair as a switch branch with no check that the arms are exclusive.
expected: //! lrm 1.3.1 + //! reject <new code> + //! xfail. Both contributions unconditional, in one block, with a comment saying the unconditionality IS the fixture - a conditional version is a legal 5.6.5 switch branch.

title: Missing negative: READING the undefined quantity of a single-nature net, as distinct from contributing to it
detail: ch1-intro.html line 123: 'only those signals types declared on the ports are accessible in the body of the model.' W05/W11 pin the write side; a compiler can reject the write and permit the read. Merged from the uncovered lens's two proposed files into one - the flow-only mirror adds no new machinery and the read-side sentence is the softer of the two clauses.
expected: //! lrm 1.3.5 + //! reject <new code> + //! xfail. One file: `voltage vonly; real x; analog begin x = I(vonly); V(vonly) <+ 1.0; end`. Low priority - write it after the write-side pair exists.

title: Missing coverage that catches a LIVE bug: I(n,p) must be -I(p,n), and VerA returns 0
detail: ch1-intro.html line 39: 'A positive flow enters a branch through the port marked with the plus sign and exits through the port marked with the minus sign.' The potential half V(n,p) == -V(p,n) is covered five times over across the suite; the flow half is covered nowhere. I WROTE AND RAN the fixture: with the branch flow held at 0.125, `I(p,n)` reads 0.125 (ok=1) but `I(n,p)` reads 0, not -0.125 (ok=0) - the residual dump shows VerA minted a SECOND unknown, `flowZ28nZ2cpZ29`, instead of negating the first. That is a real conformance bug this chapter currently cannot see. Highest-value item in the coverage block for that reason.
expected: //! lrm 1.3.1.2, hold the branch flow at 0.125, `CHECKX("flow p to n", I(p,n), 0.125)` and `CHECKX("reversing the terminals reverses the flow", I(n,p), -0.125)`, with `V(p,n) <+ 200.0*I(p,n)` so the branch is a potential source and the flow is a genuine unknown. Both literals dyadic, exact. It FAILS today, so it needs the ch01-W04 decision or a VerA fix.

title: 02 cannot tell a `ground` net from an unbiased one; bias the ground and assert it stays zero
detail: The whole content of 1.3.1.1 is that a `ground` net is zero regardless. The fixture biases only V(p), so gnd sits at the harness default of zero and every assertion passes with the `ground gnd;` line deleted. I RAN both versions: with `//! bias V(p)=0.75, V(gnd)=3.0`, the ground declaration present gives `V(gnd) got=0 ok=1` and `V(p,gnd) got=0.75 ok=1`; with the `ground gnd;` line removed the same file gives got=3 and got=-2.25, both ok=0. So the rewrite is both feasible and discriminating - it is the difference between an assertion that can fail for its stated reason and one that cannot. The existing second CHECK (V(p,gnd)-1.25 == -0.5) is arithmetic on the line above it and should go.
expected: //! lrm 1.3.1.1, `//! bias V(p) = 0.75, V(gnd) = 3.0`, `CHECKX("a ground net is zero regardless of bias", V(gnd), 0.0)` and `CHECKX("potential to the zero reference", V(p, gnd), 0.75)`.

title: Missing coverage: two nets declared ground are the one global reference node
detail: ch1-intro.html line 34: 'the node associated with the net shall be the global reference node in the circuit' - singular. Three fixtures in the whole suite declare a ground (ch01_intro/02, ch03_data_types/13, annex_h_glossary/08; the uncovered lens said two) and each declares exactly one. I WROTE AND RAN the two-ground fixture with both grounds biased away from zero: V(g1,g2) got=0, V(p,g1) got=0.75, V(p,g2) got=0.75, all ok=1. Passes today and is discriminating because the biases are ignored.
expected: //! lrm 1.3.1.1, `//! bias V(p) = 0.75, V(g1) = 3.0, V(g2) = -1.0`, three CHECKX lines as above. Biasing both grounds is what makes it a test rather than a restatement of the harness default.

title: Missing coverage: a signed four-branch KPL loop; 08 only telescopes two same-direction branches
detail: Figure 1-3 states KPL as a signed sum with two branches traversed against their reference direction: '-potential1 - potential2 + potential3 + potential4 = 0'. 08_series_potentials.va sums two branches traversed the same way, which is subtraction telescoping and cannot detect a sign error on a reversed traversal. I WROTE AND RAN the four-branch loop: all five CHECKX lines ok=1.
expected: //! lrm 1.3.2, `//! bias V(a)=1.0, V(b)=0.25, V(c)=-0.5, V(d)=0.125`; V(a,b)=0.75, V(b,c)=0.75, V(c,d)=-0.625, V(d,a)=-0.875, and the loop sum exactly 0.0. Every bias dyadic, every difference and the total exact in binary64 (verified with Fraction arithmetic).

title: Nothing in ch01 asserts the 1.3.1.2 sign convention, though COVERAGE.md credits 03 with it
detail: COVERAGE.md maps 1.3.1.2 to 03 with the note that it 'names (a,b) and probes/contributes to that same branch' - which is not a polarity claim. 03 asserts V(path_ab)==0.5 and then that same value divided by 50. A compiler that silently swapped + and - passes every fixture in the chapter. The reversed-potential check is one line and exact at the existing biases.
expected: Add `CHECKX("reversing the orientation negates the potential", V(b, a), -0.5)` and replace the /50.0 line with `CHECKEQ("the named branch and its node pair agree", V(path_ab), V(a,b), 1e-15)` - the legitimate CHECKEQ case, an identity with no value to write down. Cite //! lrm 1.3.1.2.

title: 04's digits are right but the rule is wrong: it tests 5.6.1.3 additivity, not KFL, and asserts hand arithmetic either way
detail: Both wants recomputed in binary64 and exact (2.0*(0.5-0.2)/1000.0 == 6.0e-4; the sum == 1.4e-3), so nothing is to be changed numerically. But 1.3.2's KFL is about the flows out of a NODE summing to zero; what produces 1.4e-3 is 5.6.1.3 value retention ('multiple contributions to the same potential branch or same flow branch will be additive'). And neither CHECK observes the two `<+` statements at all - both evaluate expressions the fixture writes out itself, so a compiler whose second `<+` OVERWROTE the first prints ok=1 on every line. Under //! lrm this file would advertise 1.3.2 coverage while testing chapter 5.
expected: Keep the digits. Cite `//! lrm 5.6.1.3` (and 5.6.1.2), fix the header prose, and stop crediting 1.3.2 to this file in COVERAGE.md (see ch01-W24). Making it actually observe accumulation needs a runner directive that asserts one residual entry with the same ok= discipline as CHECK - out of scope here; say so rather than implying coverage.

title: Missing coverage: ground is legal on any continuous discipline, not just electrical
detail: ch1-intro.html line 34: 'Any net of continuous discipline can be declared to be ground ... This is compatible with all analog disciplines.' All three ground fixtures in the suite use electrical, so a compiler that special-cased electrical would pass. I WROTE AND RAN the thermal version: ok=1. Note the directive must be `//! bias t = 400`, the bare unknown name - `//! bias Temp(t) = 400` fails with '`//!` names unknown `Temp(t)`' because tb.zig unknownName strips only V(, I( and x[.
expected: //! lrm 1.3.1.1, `thermal t, tgnd; ground tgnd;`, `//! bias t = 400`, `CHECKX("a non-electrical net can be the reference", Temp(t, tgnd), 400.0)`.

title: 07 is a 2.6.2 scale-factor test wearing a 1.3.1 filename, and it duplicates ch02
detail: Its only assertion is `CHECKX("scale factor m is 1e-3", 1m, 1.0e-3)`. VERIFIED duplicate: ch02_lexical/07_si_scale_factors.va:25 already asserts `CHECKX("m is milli", 1m, 0.001)`. Nothing about a flow source is asserted - no bias, no probe, no residual claim - and stripping the scale-factor line leaves a fixture that asserts nothing.
expected: Give it the 1.3.1 claim its name promises - a flow source is independent of the node potentials - by biasing the nodes and asserting the contributed value is the same number at both points, or delete the file (06_voltage_source.va already covers the source-residual pattern and ch02 owns the scale factor). Deletion is the smaller diff.

title: 05 and 10 hand-encode VerA's name mangling in a //! directive, and their first CHECK echoes the sweep
detail: Both files write `//! sweep flowZ28pZ2cnZ29 = ...` and both headers admit it ('codegen spells with its punctuation escaped'). VERIFIED in tb.zig:234: unknownName strips only `V(`, `I(` and `x[`, so `//! sweep I(p,n) = 0.02` resolves to the unknown `p,n` and would not name the branch flow at all. The escaping is a VerA codegen detail with no basis in the LRM, so these two fixtures are unportable by construction; and in both, the first CHECK's got and want are the same number routed through the directive parser and the source.
expected: Teach tb.zig's directive grammar the source-level spelling `//! sweep I(p,n) = 0.02` (it already parses V(p,n) for bias; the blocker is only that parseBindings splits bias lines on commas) and drop the mangled names from both files. Then reframe 05's echo line as harness plumbing or delete it, keeping the 3.4 parameter-default claim. This also unblocks ch01-W02, which needs a flow sweep. Touches 05, 10 and src/backend/tb.zig.

title: COVERAGE.md claims coverage it does not have and describes VerA's behavior as if it were the standard
detail: Four defects, all verified. (a) 1.2's 'contributions only inside analog' is credited to 'every behavioral fixture places <+ only in analog' - the definition of non-coverage for a prohibition. The checkable form is ch05_analog_behavior/analog_initial_contribution.va (E0405, 5.2.1); the digital-context form belongs to ch07. (b) 1.3.2's KFL is credited to 04, which tests 5.6.1.3 additivity (see W20), and the node-level law is not observable in a harness that evaluates residuals at a pinned operating point and never solves. (c) the 1.3.4/1.3.5 rows say 'pin the current custom-access ABI boundary' and 'records VerA's present custom-access ABI boundary' - the author's own statement that the fixtures beneath are behavior snapshots. (d) three rules must be listed as untestable rather than credited: 1.3's single-node-per-signal and 1.3.5's structural-only ports both need module instantiation, which VerA refuses with E0204; and 1.3.1's 'a flow probe forces the branch potential to zero' cannot be asserted at all, because reading that potential while the flow appears in an expression is itself the 1.3.1 violation W12 pins.
expected: Rewrite the 1.2, 1.3.2, 1.3.4 and 1.3.5 rows against the fixtures W01-W23 leave behind; cite ch05's fixture by path for 1.2; add an explicit 'not testable in this harness, and why' list for the three rules in (d). Do it in the same commit as W01-W05 or the file will describe fixtures that no longer exist.

title: No fixture in ch01_intro carries a //! lrm cite
detail: VERIFIED by grep: zero of the 14 .va files contain `lrm`. The contract makes `//! lrm` the only mechanical backing for a coverage claim (`torture -- --coverage`), and a failing fixture prints its cites so the report names the RULE. Every item above specifies the cite its file needs; this is the sweep for the ones no other item touches (01, 06, 08, 09).

title: Delete the four .expected-error.txt sidecars
detail: README line 3: '859 .va files. One runner. No sidecar files' and 'there is no second file to drift out of step with it'. 11/12/13/14 each carry a one-line copy of their `//! reject` value. They are dead weight now and a live drift hazard the moment W01-W05 land, at which point three of them name a verdict that no longer exists.
expected: Delete 11_potential_signal_flow.expected-error.txt, 12_flow_signal_flow.expected-error.txt, 13_mixed_conservative_signal_flow.expected-error.txt, 14_signal_flow_illegal_quantity.expected-error.txt. Four files, no other change.

title: 08's header claims two subtractions are exact in binary64; neither is
detail: The wants (1.5 twice) are correct and pass with residual 0.0. The justification is not: VERIFIED with exact rational arithmetic that double(1.0)-double(0.3) is NOT representable (it rounds to double(0.7), a half-ulp tie), and neither is double(0.3)-double(-0.5). The comparisons hold; the reasoning does not, and a reader who copies it to a different pair of biases gets burned.
expected: Either fix the prose ('each subtraction rounds to the nearest double, and the sum lands on 1.5') or make the claim true with dyadic biases V(p)=1.0, V(mid)=0.25, V(n)=-0.5 - every step then exact and CHECKX honest.

title: 09 is the only ch01 fixture with a nonzero FP residual; note it so nobody tightens the tolerance
detail: VERIFIED: 0.8-0.1 == 0.7000000000000001, 1.110e-16 above double(0.7), about 11% of the 1e-15 budget; the second check is exact only because the two errors cancel. Everything else in the chapter lands exactly, so a future sweep that promotes ch01 to CHECKX would break this file. Not an error - a trap marker.
expected: Keep the wants 0.7 / -0.4 and TOL 1e-15. Add one comment line saying the tolerance is load-bearing here, unlike the rest of the chapter. Or move to dyadic biases (0.875 / 0.125 / 0.5) and make it exact.
